s: an unfinished Chinese cultural centre and hotel standing empty beside the E4
w: A Swedish-Chinese businessman's ambitious plan to turn a roadside hotel into a grand Chinese cultural and business centre -- complete with a replica Terracotta Army and a miniature Great Wall -- got as far as an opened museum in 2008 before the hotel wing failed Swedish safety approval and the project stalled. What's left sits by the E4 highway, half-realised and empty, one of the odder things to find in rural Sweden.
_facts: Originally the Hotel Älvkarlen, built 1986, in Älvkarleby Municipality beside the E4 near Gävle
Bought and renamed "Dragon Gate" in 2004 by businessman Li Jingchun, aiming for a Sweden-China cultural/business centre
First phase, including a museum with replica Terracotta Army figures and a miniature Great Wall, opened in 2008
The intended hotel building never passed Swedish safety regulations and stands unused
